issues.legal_issue: Rent accrued under a pre-partition lease for the exclusive purposes of a successor province is allocated under the rule governing contracts made for a predecessor province, rather than the exception for other financial obligations.
material_facts: The predecessor province entered into a lease before partition, agreeing to pay monthly rent and its share of municipal taxes.
The leased premises were to be used for a purpose that, after partition, was exclusively a purpose of the successor province.
Rent and other amounts had accrued before partition, and the successor province disputed liability for amounts attributable to that period.
The successor province appealed the decree holding it liable for the disputed amounts.
issues.conclusion: The liability to pay rent under the lease was not an “other financial obligation” within Article 9. The successor province was liable under Article 8(2)(a) for rent accrued before partition, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Articles 8(2)(a) and 8(6) of the Indian Independence (Rights, Property and Liabilities) Order, 1947, a contract made for a predecessor province is treated as made for the successor province when, after partition, it serves that successor province exclusively, and accrued liabilities under it follow that allocation unless Article 9 applies. Reading “other financial obligations” ejusdem generis with loans and guarantees, Article 9 concerns obligations of a similar nature, not ordinary rent payable under a lease. The Court referred to section 178 of the Government of India Act, 1935, as contextual support, and to Province of West Bengal v. Midnapur Zemindari Co., Ltd., Sree Sree Iswar Madan Gopal Jiu v. Province of West Bengal, and The State of Punjab v. L. Mohan Lal Bhayana.

rule.if: provincial_succession_liability_appeal and predecessor_contract and contract_for_exclusive_successor_purpose and lease_rent_claim and rent_accrued_before_partition

predicates.provincial_succession_liability_appeal: A government appealed a judgment assigning to a successor province liabilities under a contract made for a predecessor province.
predicates.predecessor_contract: The predecessor province made the contract before the territorial division that created the successor province.
predicates.contract_for_exclusive_successor_purpose: After the division, the contract served purposes exclusively belonging to the successor province.
predicates.lease_rent_claim: The claimed contractual liability was rent payable under a lease.
predicates.rent_accrued_before_partition: The rent claimed had accrued before the territorial division.

issues.definition: When a government appeals the allocation of a predecessor province’s contractual liability, and the contract exclusively serves the successor province while the claim is for rent accrued before the division, the successor province bears that accrued rent liability.
